SE3.description: Sweden Bidding Zone 3 (South-central Sweden, includes Stockholm)
SE3.note: Sweden's only nuclear zone (nuclear 63.1% of 2025 generation).

SE4.note: Lower bound: 14.95% of generation is ENTSO-E 'Other' (mostly biomass/waste CHP), which has no factor in carbon_intensity_per_source.json and is counted at 0.

NO2.note: Hydro-dominated, with pumped storage and a small offshore wind share.

NO4.note: Fossil gas (3.63% of 2025 generation at 743 gCO2eq/kWh) contributes about half of this value. The gas share varies between years (near 0 in 2021, 6.23% in 2024, 3.63% in 2025), so the value is period-dependent.

metadata.source: SE1-SE4, NO1-NO5: ENTSO-E Transparency, Actual Generation per Production Type (A75), per bidding zone, full year 2025. FI: prior value, unchanged.
metadata.method: Production-based generation mix: energy-weighted average over the year of each production type's share multiplied by its factor from CodeCarbon's carbon_intensity_per_source.json. Production types with no entry in that table (ENTSO-E 'Other', 'Other renewable', 'Waste', 'Biomass') stay in the denominator with factor 0, so each value is a complete gCO2eq/kWh factor over all zone generation; the per-zone 'coverage' field gives the share that has a factor. Where coverage is well below 100% the value is a lower bound. Not consumption-based: the Electricity Maps API path remains the consumption-based source when a token is configured.
metadata.provenance: Derived reproducibly by Khepri v1.3 (avalyset/khepri), archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22285397. Method described in https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29717. Note that the archived record and the paper also publish these zones on an IPCC AR5 factor basis; those figures are not the ones shipped here.
metadata.notes: SE1-SE4 and NO1-NO5 replace the previous uniform 18.0 gCO2eq/kWh placeholder, which was below the lowest factor in carbon_intensity_per_source.json (26 for hydro and wind) and therefore unreachable for any generation mix. The Swedish zones cluster at 24.7-27.0 because hydro and wind share the same factor; the Norwegian spread (25.8-51.7) is driven by NO4's fossil-gas share.
